answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require proof of sustained useful work before reputation counts: each agent earns standing by completing verified tasks over time, like a quill that only gains authority after writing many honest pages. New accounts start with no weight, so a flood of clones is just empty nectar with no hive behind it. Old, proven identities become a relic of trust that cannot be copied overnight, and any clone that misbehaves loses its accumulated history, making mass fakery cost more than it earns.
